text:
lance: Heads-up — our canary for the new routing policy is showing a weird skew: cohort B is getting ~68% of requests instead of the configured 50/50. noticed in the dashboard around 09:02 UTC.

miriam: whoa. is that traffic at the edge or in the balancer metrics?

lance: Both. Console per-route split = 50/50, but per-instance request counts show a big imbalance.

raj: can you paste the rollout config? maybe weights didn't roll out to all routers.

lance: here's the canary policy we pushed (fresh deploy at 08:58):
```json
{"policy":"hash_by_user_id","buckets":2,"weights":{"A":50,"B":50},"salt":"v2-policy"}
```

anita: we changed hashing to modulo of the shard id earlier. could be interaction with the new consistent-hash lib.

miriam: telemetry-bot attached the metric snapshot earlier — shows cohort B higher latency but also much higher qps.

telemetry-bot: snapshot: canary.canary123.routeQPS: A=3200, B=6100; per-route-errors: A=0.2%, B=0.35% (last 15m)

gabe: sample ratio mismatch => all A/B metrics will be biased. we should pause the canary until we confirm source.

lance: agree. I've put a temp hold on progressive ramp in console. deploy-bot reports no active in-progress canary steps.

deploy-bot: action: hold-rollout executed by lance at 09:10 UTC

raj: quick diagnostic ideas: 1) check router-version on nodes that get B-heavy traffic 2) replay assignment code locally for user_ids observed in logs 3) look for duplicate header or cookie that changes hash input

anita: adding: we recently started injecting a trace-id prefix into the header for debug, could affect hashing if the code uses the whole header instead of user_id.

miriam: timeline: config pushed 08:58, console acknowledged 08:59, skew first appears 09:02. short window — likely config rollout + new hashing lib mismatch.

gabe: stat-sig note: we should not run standard t-tests here until assignment is random. Also agree to require min N per cohort before evaluating. Typical end-criteria: min 1000 users per cohort and stable weights for 10 minutes.

lance: in the short term I propose: 1) keep hold, 2) roll back hashing lib on a small subset of routers to baseline, 3) re-run assignment audit against full user_id sample, 4) only then resume.

raj: +1. For analysis, use chi-square on counts for assignment vs expected. If p < 0.001 it's significant. But we should also check stratified buckets (region, shard).

anita: I'll grep logs for header keys and run a small script to emulate the new hash function. putting results in #eng-platform-debug once done.

miriam: should we mark any metrics as invalid for this canary window (08:58-09:12)? ops and product need to know not to act on this.

lance: yes — mark window as contaminated. Gabe, can you add a note on the canary dashboard and disable alerts for it?

gabe: done. I added a banner: "Assignment skew detected — metrics in 08:58-09:12 UTC are contaminated; analysis in progress." Alerts silenced for this canary.

telemetry-bot: anomaly alert cleared by gabe at 09:18 UTC (muted).

raj: post-mortem checklist: reproduce locally, run assignment audit (script), ensure hash function uses canonical user_id only, add integration test that simulates config rollout across routers, add canary guard that checks sample ratio every 1m and auto-holds if ratio outside 55/45 for >2mins.

anita: quick repro findings: the new lib strips trailing whitespace differently, and our header concat was including `x-trace-id` when present. that changes hash for ~22% of users. pushing a patch to ignore trace header in hash input.

lance: great. timeline for revert/patch?

anita: patch ready, will deploy to 10% of routers for validation at 10:05 UTC.

miriam: once validated, let's also change end-criteria in rollout UX: require stable sample ratio (within 52/48) for 5 consecutive minutes before analytics window starts. makes sense?

gabe: agree — default should be stricter to avoid false positives. Flagging as a product change request.

lance: ok folks — action items: anita deploys patch to subset, raj runs assignment audit, miriam updates canary policy doc and FR. gabe annotates dashboard. we'll reconvene once router subset is up and we have 10m of stable metrics.

anita: deploying now. will post outcome.

lance: thanks. keeping thread open.

anita: update (10:12 UTC): subset rollout looks good — A=49.8%, B=50.2% for last 7m on patched routers. no latency regressions.

raj: audit results coming in: global chi-square p < 1e-12 before patch, after excluding patched routers p ~ 0.45. looks solid.

miriam: ok to resume? I'd prefer a gradual resume with the new guard enabled.

gabe: re-enabled progressive ramp with guard: auto-hold if ratio outside 52/48 for 3m. starting slow ramp to 10% now.

deploy-bot: ramp-step: to 10% executed by gabe at 10:22 UTC

lance: thanks team. I'll file a short postmortem and link the audit. closing thread when doc is up.

miriam: thanks all :thumbsup:
